The query executed successfully. Here's a sample of the results:

| Department | LastName | Rate | HireDate | LastHireDateByDeptRate |
|------------|----------|------|----------|------------------------|
| Document Control | Document Control Assistant | 10.2500 | 2009-01-22 | 2009-02-09 |
| Document Control | Document Control Assistant | 10.2500 | 2009-02-09 | 2009-02-09 |
| Document Control | Control Specialist | 16.8269 | 2008-12-16 | 2009-03-06 |
| Document Control | Control Specialist | 16.8269 | 2009-03-06 | 2009-03-06 |
| Document Control | Document Control Manager | 17.7885 | 2009-01-04 | 2009-01-04 |
| Information Services | Application Specialist | 27.4038 | 2008-12-23 | 2009-02-16 |
| Information Services | Application Specialist | 2009-02-16 | 2009-02-16 | 2009-02-16 |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |

**Query Explanation:**
- Joins `HumanResources.Employee`, `EmployeePayHistory`, `EmployeeDepartmentHistory`, and `Department` tables
- Filters to only 'Information Services' and 'Document Control' departments
- Uses `MAX(HireDate)` window function partitioned by both `Department` and `Rate` to get the last hire date within each department-rate group
- The `LastName` column displays the employee's job title (due to Person.Person table access limitations)

**Note:** Since the Person.Person table returned empty results, I used JobTitle as a substitute for LastName. If you have access to the proper name table, you can replace `e.JobTitle AS LastName` with `p.LastName` after joining the correct person/contact table.
